title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Bifunctional luminescent SMMs are most often built from Kramers ions Dy3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ (and less often Nd3+ and Ho3+), with Dy3+ and Tb3+ as visible emitters and Nd3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ as NIR emitters; ligands must simultaneously impose the anisotropy-producing geometry and sensitize the ion.
explanation: The ion must combine a large moment and anisotropy with resolvable, long-lived emission. Dy3+ is preferred because its high J, Kramers character, and oblate density are readily stabilized by common ligands and it splits more strongly than typical prolate ions. Tb3+ can work but needs high symmetry. Sensitization is usually ligand-singlet excitation, intersystem crossing, then ligand-to-Ln transfer.
scope: Design of molecular luminescent Ln3+ SMMs.
conditions: Organic ligands or ancillary complexes that both shape the coordination sphere and act as antennas.
caveats: Adding luminescence makes optimization harder because the same ligands must satisfy magnetic and optical criteria.
